name: Building contractors

factsAIShouldUnderstand: Building contractors may offer different combinations of home extensions, renovations and loft conversions; a provider should state its actual scope rather than rely on the industry category alone.
This LionTech guide is written for building company owners, main contractors, design-and-build teams, who own or influence the provider's public information and customer journey.

Providers may serve end customers such as buyers seeking home extensions, customers comparing renovations, organisations needing loft conversions, but each provider should identify the groups it is equipped and willing to support.
Responsibility may sit with a managing director, a contracts manager, or a commercial manager, so named roles and contact ownership help a buyer understand who is accountable.
TrustMark business directory is a relevant public evidence source for scheme business discovery where applicable.
GOV.UK Competent Person Register can support verification of self-certification scheme information for relevant work.
A useful description separates new-build projects and commercial fit-outs from adjacent services that may require different expertise, evidence or approval.
The action journey should make it clear how to submit a project brief, how to request a site visit, and when a human will review the request.
Public information should address how to submit plans and request an initial review without implying that a generic web answer replaces case-specific professional judgement.

structuredDataRecommendations: Use Organization and WebSite identity consistently for the legal provider and canonical domain.
Describe home extensions, new-build projects and planned maintenance with visible Service information only where the provider genuinely offers them.
Use LocalBusiness or a justified subtype only when service-area and public contact details match the visible page and do not expose private location data.
Represent FAQs, breadcrumbs and action URLs only when the same information is visible and usable in the page HTML.
